messages:
Maya: Quick follow-up from the RFC review — we still need to decide whether to pursue shard-level batch compaction or keep per-tenant queues and add smarter packing heuristics. I sketched tradeoffs in the doc but wanted quick takes before a design PR.

Leo: TL;DR: compaction reduces fragment-induced small batches but adds CPU overhead and GC-like pauses. per-tenant queues are simpler for isolation but waste slots.

Anika: Agree with Leo. One thing missing from the RFC: how compaction interacts with KV-cache pinning. If we compact across tenants we might evict hot KV entries more aggressively. That could spike cold-start token latency.

Raj: +1. Also worried about tail latency when compaction runs on the same core as the fastpath. We saw ~200ms p99 blips during the last probe when a background shard scan ran. :grimacing:

Maya: Good points. My thinking: two knobs — compaction frequency (epoch length) and compaction locality (per-shard vs global). We can keep compaction async on lower-priority cores and limit tokens processed per epoch. That reduces pause amplitude but increases fragmentation residue.

Leo: That sounds reasonable. We should quantify: cost = cpu_cycles(compaction_per_epoch) and benefit = tokens_saved_per_sec. If benefit < cost for a tenant class we should skip compaction for them. Maybe use a cheap classifier (rate + median seq length) to opt-out.

Anika: We can piggyback on existing telemetry: tenant_token_rate and seq_len_hist. Add a daily ranking job to compute compaction ROI per tenant class. Runtime could consult a small table.

Raj: Operationally, per-tenant queues give nice backpressure guarantees. If we compact across tenants we need a stronger admission contract to avoid starvation for low-throughput tenants during a compaction pass.

Maya: I sketched three modes in the doc: "noop" (no compaction), "local-compaction" (compact within a shard's active windows), and "cross-tenant-compact" (aggressive, full-shard packing). Proposal: default to local-compaction with adaptive epoch and a safety cap on CPU. Cross-tenant only on dedicated nodes or as part of offline maintenance windows. Thoughts?

Leo: Sounds safe. For dedicated nodes we can schedule cross-tenant compaction during low utilization windows and throttle based on observed p95 latency. We should also expose a per-tenant opt-out flag for privacy/tenancy reasons.

Anika: On implementation: compaction should operate on a write-on-merge path that yields small compaction units (micro-compact) rather than large sweeps. Pseudocode: 

```
for window in shard.windows:
  if window.age > min_age and window.size < threshold:
    try_compact(window, budget_tokens)
```

This keeps latency impact bounded. budget_tokens is the per-epoch cap.

Raj: Can we reuse the existing headroom ledger for compaction budgeting? That would unify admission signals (enqueue credits vs compaction credits). If headroom low, compaction pauses.

Maya: Good idea — reuse ledger. Also add a telemetry tag compaction.{skipped|ran}. That will let Optimize recommend configs.

Leo: Edge case: packing changes the amortized token cost and may affect cost-aware routing. We need to recompute model-selection heuristics when packing rates change by >10%. Otherwise risk routing using stale cost estimates.

Anika: True. Add a summary metric pack_ratio = packed_tokens / raw_tokens per shard pushed to the planner. Planner triggers re-eval when pack_ratio delta > threshold.

Raj: One operational ask: add a compaction kill-switch in Console (global + per-cluster). Also a readout of current compaction backlog and next-epoch ETA. Helps oncall triage during regressions.

Maya: I'll add console controls. Action items: 1) Maya to update RFC with three-mode default and ledger integration. 2) Anika to prototype micro-compact loop with budget_tokens and expose pack_ratio metric. 3) Leo to add planner hook for pack_ratio and a small ROI classifier. 4) Raj to design console kill-switch and backlog telemetry.

deploy-bot: Build queued: CI pipeline for repo inference/batcher (PR #4523). Results will be posted to this thread.

Leo: One more experiment idea: A/B users by tenant class — run aggressive compaction for 10% traffic on dedicated nodes and compare p50/p99 + cost-per-token. If p99 improves and cost drops, we can consider wider rollout.

Maya: Love it. Let's aim to land the RFC update + small prototype by EOW and schedule the A/B for the next maintenance slot. If anyone has objections or wants to take a task, say so now. :+1:

Anika: I'll take the prototype.

Raj: I'll wire the console bits after the prototype has pack_ratio telemetry.

Leo: I'll hack the planner hook and the daily ROI job.

Maya: Great — thanks all. I'll update the RFC and tag the draft PR.
